answer: A trust graph that weights attestations by social distance stops bulk fake identities from validating each other. A new identity needs six independent clusters in the shared garden of established agents, each staking 15 credits. Neighbours within two hops count near zero, so a clique cannot certify itself. When a gale of registrations comes from one source, they count as one cluster. Remote falcon verifiers slash clusters caught renting attestations. The kth fake needs six fresh clusters, so 1,000 fakes lock 90,000 credits, while an honest agent pays 90 once.
